api_healthy.description:
APIHealthy is the read-only API-liveness proof (every non-agent-role
RUNNING install — review M1): `k3s kubectl get --raw=/readyz` with a
short in-kubectl timeout. false = not proven (agent role has no local
API to ask, or the API did not answer).

node_token_hash.description:
NodeTokenHash is the SHA256 hex of the k3s server join token
(/var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/node-token) — the cluster-identity
fingerprint the adopt decision's one-cluster rule compares. The HASH
only: the raw token never crosses the wire. "" when the file is
absent. A token that exists but cannot be fingerprinted (unreadable,
sha256sum missing) FAILS the whole probe (non-zero exit → the caller's
fail-closed probe_unavailable path) — it must never read as an empty
fingerprint that vacuously "agrees" with another member's.

role.description:
Role classifies the install: RoleServer or RoleAgent; "" when no data
dir was seen (the unit + pgrep evidence still speak).

unit.description:
Unit is the systemd unit found ACTIVE: "k3s.service" (server) or
"k3s-agent.service" (worker). "" when nothing is active or the guest is
systemd-less (the pgrep fallback cannot name a unit).

arch.description: Arch is the node architecture: amd64 | arm64.

claimed_hosts.description:
ClaimedHosts are the route hostnames other installs on this cluster
already claim — the fact the hostname-uniqueness preflight (EDGE.md
§4 rule 1) checks route hosts against; a collision refuses naming the
conflicting install. The HOST keeps this registry authoritative
(record on provision, release on uninstall); omitempty keeps legacy
facts byte-identical.

data_disk_fs.description:
DataDiskFS is the host data-disk filesystem (the frozen DataDiskFS
vocabulary). Continuous FILE sync requires a CoW snapshot
layer — on plain ext4 the resolve-time check refuses it
(STORAGE.md §3).

destinations.description:
Destinations are the backup destinations the platform's destination
registry offers as viable for this install (user's buckets, probed
reachable). A durability.destination outside this set is refused at
resolve (ErrCapabilityUnavailable).

domains.description: Domains are the manageable zones for env_local hostnames.

gateway.description:
Gateway is the cluster's edge-gateway publish fact (story 130.2,
EDGE.md §2) — the flavor the cluster runs and the address its edge
publishes. The web-class compile targets it instead of guessing: the
dns-apply instructions point here, dns-verify expects it, and
route-apply renders for its flavor. Nil when the cluster has no
gateway addon yet — a web compile refuses without it.
omitempty so pre-130.2 persisted facts re-marshal byte-identically.

node_tier.description:
NodeTier is the node's memory tier (the frozen NodeTier vocabulary).
The 1gb tier narrows durability to off/scheduled only (STORAGE.md §7).

storage_classes.description:
StorageClasses are the storage classes the platform declared on this
cluster (STORAGE.md §7 tiering is compiled FROM these). A
storage.class value outside this set is refused at resolve
(ErrCapabilityUnavailable).

flavor.description:
Flavor is the gateway flavor the cluster chose ONCE (v1 vocabulary:
caddy). The choice is sticky per cluster (EDGE.md §4 rule 3) — v1
renders caddy only; a migration is a documented re-deploy.

publish_address.description:
PublishAddress is the address the gateway's edge publishes: an IP
(A-record form) or a hostname (CNAME form — tunnel topologies). The
record type the dns steps use FOLLOWS this form.

host.description:
Host is the claimed hostname (normalized: lowercase, no trailing
dot).

install_name.description:
InstallName names the install holding the claim — the conflicting
install a uniqueness refusal names (the backend maps that refusal to
HTTP 422; the module's contract is the sentinel).

replication.description:
Replication is the class's replica factor (1 | 3); replicated
classes are refused below vendor minimums (STORAGE.md §7).

snapshot_layer.description:
SnapshotLayer marks CoW snapshot capability — required for
continuous FILE sync.

valid.description: Valid is true if Time is not NULL

ami_id.description:
Advanced options (for explicit user control)
If provided, these bypass the VM planner's decision-making

bastion_enabled.description: Story 18-7-8: SSH Security fields (Context-Based Access Control)

user_public_ips.description: Manual SSH access IPs (appended to allow list)

roles.description: vm_id -> role mapping (optional, auto-assign if omitted)

adopt_existing.description:
AdoptExisting is the EXPLICIT ADOPT opt-in (story 124.3, constraint
4): accept pre-existing, RUNNING, same-version k3s on the members
instead of installing. Without it, a member with running k3s is 409
existing_k3s_running. The server verifies EVERY member via the
contamination preflight before honoring it (verified adoption
records cluster.adopted=true; an unverified opt-in is not honored).

agent_deploy_method.description:
AgentDeployMethod selects how the k8s-agent is deployed inside the
cluster after provisioning: "kubectl" (default, applies manifest via
client-go) or "helm" (installs via Helm SDK from the chart repo).

failure_policy.description:
FailurePolicy is the E5-7 LOCKED failure policy for multi-master
creates (story 125.3): "system_managed" (per-master retries to the
deadline, then the quorum-preconditioned auto-return ladder) or
"user_managed" (hold + action_required on first failure, zero
autonomous actions). Locked for the operation; persisted with the
operation record (job payload + the D6 hold) — never a cluster
column. Multi-master only; single-master ignores it.

install_config.description:
InstallConfig overrides distribution install defaults. Keys recognized by
the distribution (e.g. "snapshotter") set the corresponding flag; unknown
keys are passed through as --key=value. Empty = use distribution defaults.

network_id.description:
NetworkID is the explicit network contract (story 124.17, D12): the
network every member VM must belong to, selected in wizard step 1.
Nullable — null = the acknowledged "No network — advanced" choice
(every member must be networkless). Validated server-side against
every member; violations surface as structured 409s
(vm_not_in_network / vm_in_cluster).

vm_ids.description:
VMIDs is the array of VM IDs for BYOV clusters. The first VM
is assigned the master role; all others are workers. For
explicit per-VM role assignment, use VMRoles instead.

vm_roles.description:
VMRoles allows explicit per-VM role assignment. When provided,
it overrides the implicit first-VM-is-master convention.
Each entry maps a VM ID to its role ("master" or "worker").
If omitted, VMIDs is used with the first element as master.

ip_address.description: Remote connection details (required only if IsLocal is false)

is_local.description: true for local machine, false for remote

purpose.description:
Purpose + DraftName carry the durable cluster-create draft intent
(story 124.17 AC7). The wizard sends purpose="cluster-create" plus the
cluster name it is heading toward; ordinary network creates omit both.
Only "cluster-create" is accepted today — anything else is stripped so
the column cannot be used as a free-text channel.

acknowledge_irreversible.description:
AcknowledgeIrreversible is the AC5 confirm-again flag (the server's
irreversibility_warning 409 carries the verbatim text; re-submit with
this true).

cluster_id.description:
ClusterID is present on the auto-install path (kubeconfig provided).
The FE uses it to navigate to the cluster detail page and subscribe
to progress events. Nil on the manual path (no cluster row yet).

vm_name.description: For VM installations (only valid with bare-metal/imported)

expiration_mode.description:
ExpirationMode + DurationMinutes carry the maintainer's dual-mode choice
(Epic 103 / ADR-078). ExpirationMode is "fixed" (default) or "sliding".
DurationMinutes sets the fixed deadline or the initial sliding window;
it defaults to 15 when unset or out of range.

remaining_backup_codes.description: Number of unused backup codes left

qr_code_url.description: otpauth://totp/... (put in an on the frontend)

credentials.description:
Credentials is ALWAYS a masked view. The list path does not even decrypt
(AC5); the create/edit paths return this same minimal placeholder.

has_vault_credentials.description:
HasVaultCredentials tells the FE whether a "rotate" affordance applies
(104.4). It does NOT leak the secret.

mfa_token.description:
MFA fields are forward-compatible (BE-X will add org MFA — see
vault_unlock_mfa.go for the user-side analog). BE-2 ignores them.

parent_connection_id.description:
Bastion/parent connection (nullable)
If set, this connection requires jumping through the parent bastion host

private_key_encrypted_data_id.description:
Encrypted SSH Key (Story 18-14: Refactored to use polymorphic encrypted_data table)
SECURITY FIX: Previously stored plaintext - now encrypted!
References the EncryptedData table where the SSH private key is stored encrypted

use_agent_forwarding.description:
SSH Agent forwarding (when using bastion)
If true, uses bastion's SSH agent instead of a separate key

enabled.description:
Enabled is true when dev mode is being turned ON, false when turned OFF.
The FE only fires this endpoint on the ON transition (the story
specifies "one-time audit signal"); we accept the field anyway so a
future caller can record the OFF transition without an API change.

action.description: seal action (e.g. "seal_sa_secret") — must be in seal policy AllowedActions

worker_key.description: hex-encoded target worker pubkey (allowlisted in seal policy)

error.example: Rate limit exceeded. Maximum: 10 jobs/minute. Try again in 45 seconds.

adopted.description:
Adopted records the D3 ADOPT decision (story 124.3, constraint 4):
creation's contamination preflight found pre-existing, RUNNING,
same-version k3s on EVERY member and the caller explicitly opted in
with adopt_existing. Adopted means BMC installed NO k3s on any member
(SetupNode's k3s step is skipped downstream); the D9 canonical
predicate bmc_installed_k3s = (origin==created && !adopted) keys on
this column, and adopted clusters are panel-only (D8).

headscale_enabled.description:
Headscale mesh networking (Story 51-2).
HeadscaleUserID added in Epic 100 Story 100-2: canonical numeric ID
assigned by Headscale at CreateUser time, persisted so the teardown
path (DisableClusterMesh / DeleteUserByID) doesn't have to derive the
name from the DB row. Mirrors Network.MeshNetworkConfig.HeadscaleUserID.
See ADR-058 for the direct-headscale cluster-mesh path.

install_config.description:
InstallConfig carries per-cluster overrides for the k8s distribution installer
(e.g. {"snapshotter":"native"} for nested-container tests). Keys not recognized
by the distribution are passed through as --key=value install flags. Empty/nil
means "use distribution defaults" — no flags are forced. This is persisted so
crash-resume and asynq retries retain the caller's intent.

k8s_version.description: Cluster metadata fields for imported clusters

operation_generation.description:
OperationGeneration is D6's serialization counter: every mutating
action CASes WHERE operation_generation = N and bumps it. Zero for
never-mutated rows. See services/cluster_operation_cas.go.

status_since.description:
StatusSince is the wall-clock of the last Status TRANSITION — the FE's
"since <time>" pill suffix truth. Stamped by the shared
RecordClusterStatusTransition helper; rows written before epic-124
carry NULL and the payload omits the field.

sub_status.description:
SubStatus is the machine-written lifecycle refinement of Status
(epic-124 story 124.5). THIS story ships the column + the type-safe
value set only — each value's WRITER lands with its own story
(124.6 installing_* / waiting_agent, 124.9 healing | deadline_exhausted,
124.10 retrying_agent + action_required resolutions). Empty string means
"no sub-state" (the value every pre-124.5 row reads back as).

phase.description:
Phase is the install-lifecycle checkpoint (resume source of truth).
Primary path (issue #1438): pending→setting_up→joining→ready, with
"failed" as a resettable terminal (stuck nodes converge to it via the
per-node timeout).

auth_mode.description:
AuthMode is the explicit auth contract (Story 79.1). Empty on legacy rows;
ResolveAuthMode() derives from Type (+ FK) until backfilled by writes.

aws_credential_id.description: For ECR: AWS credential reference and region

azure_credential_id.description: For ACR: Azure credential reference and login server (for username/password auth)

url.description: Registry endpoint (auto-filled for known types, editable for private)

username.description:
Username for basic auth (Docker Hub, GHCR, private registries)
Password is stored encrypted using polymorphic encrypted_data table

progress.description:
Fine-grained progress roll-up (0–100) and current step label.
Updated by the step writer in the same tx that writes job_steps.
List queries read these columns directly — no N+1 on job_steps.

resource_type.description:
Generic resource link (ADR-060 V6 — replaces cluster_id/vm_id).
"cluster" | "vm" | "database" | "network" | "multipass" | …

status.description:
Coarse status enum (pending → running → completed|failed|cancelled).
Status transitions are driven by a generic mechanism (ADR-060 Option A),
never hand-set by business-logic error handling.

workflow_id.description:
Temporal domain key (e.g. "provision-cluster-42").
Set when the job triggers a Temporal workflow; nil for Asynq-only jobs.

parent_connection_id.description:
Bastion/parent connection (nullable)
If set, this connection requires jumping through the parent bastion host

private_key_encrypted_data_id.description:
Encrypted SSH Key (Story 18-14: Refactored to use polymorphic encrypted_data table)
SECURITY FIX: Previously stored plaintext - now encrypted!
References the EncryptedData table where the SSH private key is stored encrypted

use_agent_forwarding.description:
SSH Agent forwarding (when using bastion)
If true, uses bastion's SSH agent instead of a separate key

is_local.description: true for local machine, false for remote

ssh_connection_id.description: Reference to ManagedSSHConnection (the jump host entry)

last_seen_at.description: Last seen tracks when the agent last reported this VM's state

draft_name.description:
DraftName is the cluster name the wizard was heading toward when the
network was created (paired with Purpose=cluster-create).

last_reconcile_at.description:
LastReconcileAt is the timestamp of the most recent reconciler touch.
Used for observability + to detect reconciler stalls.

purpose.description:
Purpose is the durable cluster-create draft intent (124.17): "" for
ordinary networks, "cluster-create" for wizard-created drafts. See the
NetworkPurpose docs. GORM AutoMigrate (dev-stage policy) adds the column
on next boot; 000055 keeps the goose path convergent.

reconcile_attempts.description:
ReconcileAttempts is incremented by the Story 101-12 Temporal reconciler
every time it retries a stuck row. When it reaches MaxReconcileAttempts
(10) the row flips to NetworkStatusErrorPermanent. GORM AutoMigrate
(dev-stage policy) adds the column on next boot.

last_node_left_at.description:
LastNodeLeftAt is stamped by the story 124.14 membership-free write when
the write removed a network's LAST network_nodes row and nothing (no
node, no cluster binding) remains — the candidate marker the network
reconciler's last-node reap pass (ReapLastNodeLeftNetworks) tears the
network down from, after a grace window. Stored INSIDE the Config JSONB
on purpose: the column is already JSONB, so the new key needs NO schema
migration and legacy rows simply read it as nil.

x-enum-comments.NetworkStatusErrorPermanent: Story 101-12: reconciler exhausted retries; needs user action
x-enum-comments.NetworkStatusRemoving: in-flight delete (A-N4); Headscale DeleteUser running async

x-enum-descriptions: in-flight delete (A-N4); Headscale DeleteUser running async
Story 101-12: reconciler exhausted retries; needs user action

default_bucket.description: Optional: Default bucket for this connection

endpoint.description:
S3 endpoint (auto-filled based on provider, editable for "other")
AWS: https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com
MinIO: https://<your-minio-host>:9000
Wasabi: https://s3.wasabisys.com
GCS: https://storage.googleapis.com

project_id.description:
Story 104.3: ProjectID is now nullable (*uint) so a row may be
org-scoped (ProjectID = nil) instead of project-scoped. The org-vs-
project distinction is one branch: `project_id IS NULL` = org-scoped.
AutoMigrate applies the NOT NULL → nullable change (dev-stage policy).

access_mode.description:
AccessMode (Epic 89 — BYOV VM Console) determines interactive-shell policy.
  byov     — user-owned VM (own_managed, user cloud key, multipass guest).
             End-user Console / SSH allowed (role-gated).
  platform — provisioned with a BMC system cloud credential
             (CloudProviderCredential.IsSystemOwned). End-user shell
             forbidden; future admin panel is a separate surface.

Default "byov" preserves existing UX for rows that predate this field
(GORM backfills the column default on AutoMigrate — dev-stage policy).

cluster_id.description:
Cluster association (optional - VM can be standalone or part of a cluster)
Note: Cascade deletion is handled at application level based on ClusterOrigin
- OriginCreated: VMs are deleted when cluster is deleted (if user opts in)
- OriginImported: VMs are never deleted automatically; only k8s is uninstalled

connection_type.description:
Polymorphic association for connection
connection_type examples: managed_ssh_connections, aws_key_pair, gcp_service_account

deletion_reason_code.description:
DeletionReasonCode is the machine-contract reason a VM removal landed in
cleanup_incomplete (issue #1454, AC3): one of the VMRemovalReason*
constants. NULL on every row not in cleanup_incomplete. The FE maps
codes → copy; unknown codes render status_reason (sanitized human
fallback detail), so the exact strings are a wire contract.

k3s_state.description:
K3SState is the guest-truth k3s lifecycle state of this VM's host
(story 124-1 AC6, epic-124): 'none' = no k3s installed on the guest;
'installed' = a successful SetupNode/uninstall-symmetric moment completed;
'unknown' = never observed (the default — rows predating the column and
guests outside cluster flows backfill nothing). Writers land ONLY at the
guest-state moments that exist today, both via WriteNodePhase (the
ADR-060 single-writer choke point): phase ready → installed,
phase removed → none. The 124.3 probe writer and the detach /
delete-keep writers arrive with their owning stories.

network_id.description: Network association (optional - VM can be part of a network)

org_id.description: Tenant scope (ADR-062): replaces the former owner-only UserID.

provider_vm_id.description: Provider-specific VM identifier (e.g., EC2 instance ID, GCP instance name, Azure VM name)

specs_status.description:
SpecsStatus is the EVIDENCE status of the CPU/RAM/disk spec columns
(story 124-2, D4): 'reported' = an agent metrics report carrying
cpu_count/memory_total_bytes/disk_total_bytes has been seen for this VM;
'unknown' = never observed (the default — no report, no inference). The
only writer after creation is the D4 projection in the metrics collector
(services.SpecProjector): create-time declared specs and the SSH display
migration are not evidence — specs_status stays 'unknown' for them. The
status is NEVER derived from the column values (never "0 means
unknown"). Consumers: cluster-create preflight (124.3) and the VM
pages' specs pill.

ssh_key_encrypted_data_id.description:
Encrypted SSH Key Storage (Polymorphic encrypted_data table)
References the EncryptedData table where the SSH private key is stored encrypted

ssh_public_key.description: SSH Access (for VMs where we provisioned SSH keys)

purpose.description:
Draft intent (story 124.17 AC7): 'cluster-create' when the wizard
created this network as a draft for the cluster named by DraftName.
Surfaces the Networks-page resume banner / "Prepared for a cluster"
chip without a per-row join-status call.

on_this_network.description:
OnThisNetwork badges selected-network members ("on N1" chip). False
for networkless candidates the wizard will PRE-JOIN.

rejection.description:
Rejection is the 124.3 server-computed preflight verdict for this VM —
the machine contract the picker cards render inline (disabled-with-
reason; the contamination card keys Adoptable). Nil/omitted = the VM
passes list-level classification; the create-time gate re-verifies with
a live probe (the list is a hint, the gate is the truth).

specs_unknown.description:
SpecsUnknown mirrors 124.2's specs contract: true while the VM's
health and specs are not yet agent-reported ("Waiting for agent data").

supported.description: Supported false = the platform cannot build this count today.

next_last.description: pass as last= on next page when Link present / truncated

stale_note.description:
StaleNote is the ENGINE's honest escalation copy wired through when
Stale is true (review MED-2) — BE-owned, rendered verbatim; empty
(omitempty) on the fresh path.

CookieAuth.description: Cookie authentication (automatic). Use the login form in the banner above - DO NOT use the Authorize button. Login with email/password or OAuth, and cookies will be set automatically.
CookieAuth.name: Cookie

EncryptionKeyAuth.description: Legacy (pre-ADR-067) security scheme name, kept only so existing @Security references stay valid. The active vault session header is X-Org-Vault-Token, issued by POST /orgs/:org_id/vault/unlock; send the session ID directly (plain UUID).
EncryptionKeyAuth.name: X-Encryption-Key

OrgIDHeader.description: Organization ID for tenant list scoping (TenantListScope / Epic 85). Required with X-Project-Id on list/index routes.
OrgIDHeader.name: X-Org-ID

ProjectIdHeader.description: Project filter for tenant list routes: a numeric project id, or the case-sensitive sentinel `all` for every project the caller can access in X-Org-ID.
ProjectIdHeader.name: X-Project-Id
